doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

chapter: Trombonists, old string bands and dance steps
title: Quadrilles, varieties and Lancers
summary: Tom explains the quadrilles and Lancers he played, with first, second and fourth figures, and says he played them for white dancers.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah. Well, that do, re, miso, las, et, oh. You see how it's like then? One, two, three, waltz and two, four times. Uh, uh, mazoka times. I used to play them old, uh, uh, varietas. I used to play
with varietas too. You don't play them the vals. Are they something like quadrilles or what were they?

Quadrilles, like quadrilles, but they have little, uh, different, uh, different movements and waltzes and everything else. Yeah, but it's the same thing. You got five, you got five forts to it. Yeah. Yeah. I used to play down in the quadrilles. I used to play on them quadrilles. First figure, second figure, and fourth figure. What were the Lancers? Were the Lancers?
The Lancers. They were the Lancers. Was that about the same as the quadrille or what does that mean? I don't even know.

Well, the Lancers, well the Lancers is about the same as, uh, no. It's, it's a kind of a different dance to Lancers. Different, different kind of a dance. Yeah. Different on the Lancers. And, uh, yes, it's a different kind. It's most like a quadrilles. But it's a little different. Yeah. You understand? It's a little different. Yeah, I see. I used to play that, you wear it. I used to play that for white. You see, the color didn't dance. They didn't dance though.
